---- MODULE W4Od6m3p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Dispatchers, Calls, Slots, MaxTerm

NoLeader == "noleader"
FreeSlot == "free"
NoSlot == "noslot"

VARIABLES term, leader, bookedFor, takenUp, net

vars == <<term, leader, bookedFor, takenUp, net>>

Grants == [call : Calls, slot : Slots, term : 0..MaxTerm]

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ leader \in Dispatchers \union {NoLeader}
    /\ bookedFor \in [Slots -> Calls \union {FreeSlot}]
    /\ takenUp \in [Calls -> Slots \union {NoSlot}]
    /\ net \subseteq Grants

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ bookedFor = [s \in Slots |-> FreeSlot]
    /\ takenUp = [k \in Calls |-> NoSlot]
    /\ net = {}

ElectDispatcher(d) ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ leader' = d
    /\ term' = IF term < MaxTerm THEN term + 1 ELSE term
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookedFor, takenUp, net>>

FailDispatcher ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ leader' = NoLeader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, bookedFor, takenUp, net>>

BookSlot(k, s) ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ bookedFor[s] = FreeSlot
    /\ takenUp[k] = NoSlot
    /\ \A g \in net : g.call # k
    /\ bookedFor' = [bookedFor EXCEPT ![s] = k]
    /\ net' = net \union {[call |-> k, slot |-> s, term |-> term]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, takenUp>>

AcceptGrant(g) ==
    /\ g \in net
    /\ g.term = term
    /\ bookedFor[g.slot] = g.call
    /\ takenUp[g.call] = NoSlot
    /\ takenUp' = [takenUp EXCEPT ![g.call] = g.slot]
    /\ net' = net \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, bookedFor>>

DiscardGrant(g) ==
    /\ g \in net
    /\ \/ g.term # term
       \/ bookedFor[g.slot] # g.call
       \/ takenUp[g.call] # NoSlot
    /\ net' = net \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, bookedFor, takenUp>>

ReleaseSlot(k) ==
    /\ takenUp[k] # NoSlot
    /\ bookedFor' = [bookedFor EXCEPT ![takenUp[k]] = FreeSlot]
    /\ takenUp' = [takenUp EXCEPT ![k] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, net>>

RevokeBooking(s) ==
    /\ bookedFor[s] # FreeSlot
    /\ takenUp[bookedFor[s]] # s
    /\ \A g \in net : g.slot # s
    /\ bookedFor' = [bookedFor EXCEPT ![s] = FreeSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, takenUp, net>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Dispatchers : ElectDispatcher(d)
    \/ FailDispatcher
    \/ \E k \in Calls, s \in Slots : BookSlot(k, s)
    \/ \E g \in Grants : AcceptGrant(g)
    \/ \E g \in Grants : DiscardGrant(g)
    \/ \E k \in Calls : ReleaseSlot(k)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : RevokeBooking(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TakenSlotIsBookedForItsCall ==
    \A k \in Calls : takenUp[k] # NoSlot => bookedFor[takenUp[k]] = k

====
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper assigns shaft time slots to waiting hall calls.
One dispatcher at a time is the elected leader, and leadership carries a term
number that advances with each election until the term counter reaches its
ceiling, after which elections install a new dispatcher under the standing term.
The installed leader can fail at any point, leaving the bank leaderless until the
next election.

Each slot records the call it is booked for, or that it is free, and each call
records the slot it has actually taken up, or that it has none. The leader books
a free slot for a call that holds no slot and has no grant already travelling: the
slot is marked as booked for that call immediately, and a grant message naming the
call, the slot, and the current term is put on the network.

The network gives no ordering guarantee, so grants sit in flight and are picked up
in any order the bank likes. When a grant is picked up, it is accepted only if its
term is still the current term, the slot it names is still booked for the call it
names, and that call has not already taken up a slot; acceptance records the slot
as the call's own. A grant that fails any of those checks is discarded.

A call that has taken up a slot can release it, freeing the slot and clearing the
call's record. The leader can also revoke a booking on a slot that its call never
took up, but only once no grant for that slot is still in flight, so a booking is
never pulled out from under a grant that is about to be accepted.

The complete set of actions is: elect a dispatcher, fail the installed dispatcher,
book a free slot for a call and put a grant on the network, accept a grant that
still passes all its checks, discard a grant that does not, release a slot a call
has taken up, and revoke an untaken booking once no grant for that slot is in
flight.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a call has taken up a slot, that slot is booked for
exactly that call, so no two calls can ever have taken up the same shaft slot.

---- MODULE W4Od14m1p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS RingSize, MaxGen, MaxFrames

Drones == 1..RingSize
Nowhere == 0
NextIn(d) == (d % RingSize) + 1

VARIABLES gen, tokenAt, believedGen, believes, crashed, frames

vars == <<gen, tokenAt, believedGen, believes, crashed, frames>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ gen \in 0..MaxGen
    /\ tokenAt \in Drones \union {Nowhere}
    /\ believedGen \in [Drones -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ believes \subseteq Drones
    /\ crashed \subseteq Drones
    /\ frames \in 0..MaxFrames

TrueHolder(d) ==
    /\ d \in believes
    /\ believedGen[d] = gen
    /\ tokenAt = d
    /\ d \notin crashed

Init ==
    /\ gen = 0
    /\ tokenAt = 1
    /\ believedGen = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ believes = {1}
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ frames = 0

PassToken(d) ==
    /\ TrueHolder(d)
    /\ tokenAt' = NextIn(d)
    /\ believes' = (believes \ {d}) \union {NextIn(d)}
    /\ believedGen' = [believedGen EXCEPT ![NextIn(d)] = gen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, crashed, frames>>

Transmit(d) ==
    /\ TrueHolder(d)
    /\ frames < MaxFrames
    /\ frames' = frames + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, tokenAt, believedGen, believes, crashed>>

CrashSilently(d) ==
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \union {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, tokenAt, believedGen, believes, frames>>

RegenerateToken(e) ==
    /\ tokenAt \in crashed
    /\ e \notin crashed
    /\ gen < MaxGen
    /\ gen' = gen + 1
    /\ tokenAt' = e
    /\ believes' = believes \union {e}
    /\ believedGen' = [believedGen EXCEPT ![e] = gen + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, frames>>

GiveUpBelief(d) ==
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ d \in believes
    /\ believedGen[d] < gen
    /\ believes' = believes \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, tokenAt, believedGen, crashed, frames>>

RestartDrone(d) ==
    /\ d \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {d}
    /\ believes' = IF believedGen[d] = gen THEN believes ELSE believes \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, tokenAt, believedGen, frames>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : PassToken(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Transmit(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : CrashSilently(d)
    \/ \E e \in Drones : RegenerateToken(e)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : GiveUpBelief(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : RestartDrone(d)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A d \in Drones : SF_vars(GiveUpBelief(d))
    /\ \A d \in Drones : SF_vars(RestartDrone(d))

CurrentBelievers == {d \in Drones : d \in believes /\ believedGen[d] = gen}

OnlyRealHolderBelievesCurrent == CurrentBelievers \subseteq {tokenAt}

StaleBeliefEventuallyResolved ==
    \A d \in Drones :
        (d \in believes /\ believedGen[d] < gen)
            ~> (d \notin believes \/ believedGen[d] = gen)

====

CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 3
    MaxGen = 2
    MaxFrames = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyRealHolderBelievesCurrent
PROPERTY StaleBeliefEventuallyResolved
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm flies in a fixed ring and shares the downlink
by passing a single token around that ring. The token has a generation number,
the swarm records which drone the token is actually at, and each drone separately
holds a belief about whether it has the token together with the generation of the
token it thinks it holds.

The token holder may transmit imagery only when it believes it holds the token,
the generation it believes is the swarm's current generation, the swarm really
does record the token as being at that drone, and the drone has not crashed. The
holder may pass the token to the next drone in the ring under the same
conditions; passing moves the recorded token, gives the next drone the belief and
the current generation, and takes the belief away from the passer.

A drone can crash silently. Nothing visible changes: it keeps its belief and its
generation, and if the token was recorded at it the token stays recorded there,
so the ring simply stops turning. When the token is stranded at a crashed drone,
ground control regenerates it: the generation advances and the token is recorded
at a chosen uncrashed drone, which is given the belief at the new generation. The
stranded drone's own belief is deliberately left alone, so it is left believing it
holds a token of a generation that no longer exists.

A drone whose believed generation is behind the swarm's current generation and
which has not crashed gives up its belief. A crashed drone can be restarted, and
on restart it gives up any belief that is not at the current generation.

The complete set of actions is: pass the token to the next drone in the ring,
transmit imagery as the true current holder, crash a drone silently, regenerate
the token onto an uncrashed drone when it is stranded at a crashed one, have a
running drone with a behind-the-times belief give that belief up, and restart a
crashed drone.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the set of drones that believe they hold a token of the swarm's
current generation is always contained in the single-element set naming the drone
the token is actually recorded at, so a stranded or superseded drone can never
pass the check that guards transmitting.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: a drone left believing it holds a token of a superseded
generation is eventually put right, either by giving that belief up or by being
handed a token of the current generation.

---- MODULE W4Od10m7p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Controllers, Blocks, MaxVersion

NoWriter == "nowriter"
Interlocking == "interlocking"

VARIABLES reg, inflight, writerOf, rejected

vars == <<reg, inflight, writerOf, rejected>>

Proposals == [by : Controllers, block : Blocks, version : 0..MaxVersion]

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [locked : SUBSET Blocks, version : 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ inflight \subseteq Proposals
    /\ writerOf \in [1..MaxVersion -> Controllers \union {Interlocking, NoWriter}]
    /\ rejected \subseteq Controllers

Init ==
    /\ reg = [locked |-> {}, version |-> 0]
    /\ inflight = {}
    /\ writerOf = [v \in 1..MaxVersion |-> NoWriter]
    /\ rejected = {}

ProposeBlock(c, b) ==
    /\ \A m \in inflight : m.by # c
    /\ inflight' = inflight \union
                    {[by |-> c, block |-> b, version |-> reg.version]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, writerOf, rejected>>

ApplyProposal(m) ==
    /\ m \in inflight
    /\ m.version = reg.version
    /\ m.version < MaxVersion
    /\ reg' = [locked |-> reg.locked \union {m.block},
               version |-> m.version + 1]
    /\ writerOf' = [writerOf EXCEPT ![m.version + 1] = m.by]
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED rejected

RejectProposal(m) ==
    /\ m \in inflight
    /\ \/ m.version # reg.version
       \/ reg.version = MaxVersion
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
    /\ rejected' = rejected \union {m.by}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, writerOf>>

ReleaseBlock(b) ==
    /\ b \in reg.locked
    /\ reg.version < MaxVersion
    /\ reg' = [locked |-> reg.locked \ {b}, version |-> reg.version + 1]
    /\ writerOf' = [writerOf EXCEPT ![reg.version + 1] = Interlocking]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, rejected>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, b \in Blocks : ProposeBlock(c, b)
    \/ \E m \in Proposals : ApplyProposal(m)
    \/ \E m \in Proposals : RejectProposal(m)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : ReleaseBlock(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WriteHistoryHasNoGap ==
    \A v \in 1..reg.version : writerOf[v] # NoWriter

====
nl:
A subway signalling block system keeps its shared record, the set of track blocks
currently locked, in a single compare-and-swap register. The register carries the
locked set together with a version number. Alongside the register the system
keeps a write history: for each version number it records who performed the write
that produced it, or records that nothing produced it yet.

Interlocking controllers ask for a block by putting a proposal on the network. A
proposal names the controller, the block it wants, and the register version the
controller read when it built the proposal. A controller may have at most one
proposal in flight, and it may ask for any block at all. The network gives no
ordering guarantee, so proposals sit in flight and are taken up in whatever order
the interlocking gets to them; a block a controller wanted may well already be
locked by the time its proposal is taken up, in which case applying the proposal
simply leaves that block locked.

Taking up a proposal is a compare-and-swap. The proposal is applied only if the
version it carries is still the register's version and the version counter has
room left; applying adds the block to the locked set, sets the register's version
to one past the version the proposal carried, and records the proposing
controller as the writer of that new version. A proposal whose version no longer
matches, or that arrives when the version counter is exhausted, is rejected and
its proposing controller is noted as having been rejected.

The interlocking itself can release a locked block. A release also writes the
register: it removes the block from the locked set, advances the version by one,
and records the interlocking as the writer of that new version.

The complete set of actions is: put a proposal for a block on the network, apply a proposal whose version still matches, reject a proposal that no
longer qualifies, and release a locked block as the interlocking.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every version number from one up to the register's current
version has a writer recorded against it, so the write history has no gap and no
accepted write has ever been overwritten by a proposal built on a version that
had already moved on.

---- MODULE W4Od17m9p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bags, Lanes, PerLane, MaxEpoch

Outside == "outside"
Riding == "riding"
Aside == "aside"
Delivered == "delivered"

VARIABLES epoch, activeLanes, place, seized

vars == <<epoch, activeLanes, place, seized>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ activeLanes \subseteq Lanes
    /\ place \in [Bags -> {Outside, Riding, Aside, Delivered}]
    /\ seized \in BOOLEAN

RidingCount == Cardinality({b \in Bags : place[b] = Riding})
CapacityOf(ls) == Cardinality(ls) * PerLane

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ activeLanes = Lanes
    /\ place = [b \in Bags |-> Outside]
    /\ seized = FALSE

AdmitBag(b) ==
    /\ place[b] = Outside
    /\ RidingCount + 1 <= CapacityOf(activeLanes)
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![b] = Riding]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, activeLanes, seized>>

DeliverBag(b) ==
    /\ place[b] = Riding
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![b] = Delivered]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, activeLanes, seized>>

RecycleBag(b) ==
    /\ place[b] = Delivered
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![b] = Outside]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, activeLanes, seized>>

Reconfigure(ls) ==
    /\ ~seized
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ ls # activeLanes
    /\ RidingCount <= CapacityOf(ls)
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ activeLanes' = ls
    /\ UNCHANGED <<place, seized>>

SeizeRouter ==
    /\ ~seized
    /\ seized' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, activeLanes, place>>

ReleaseRouter ==
    /\ seized
    /\ seized' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, activeLanes, place>>

ForceLaneSet(ls) ==
    /\ seized
    /\ activeLanes' = ls
    /\ place' = [b \in Bags |-> IF place[b] = Riding THEN Aside ELSE place[b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, seized>>

LetBackIn(b) ==
    /\ place[b] = Aside
    /\ RidingCount + 1 <= CapacityOf(activeLanes)
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![b] = Riding]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, activeLanes, seized>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Bags : AdmitBag(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : DeliverBag(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : RecycleBag(b)
    \/ \E ls \in SUBSET Lanes : Reconfigure(ls)
    \/ SeizeRouter
    \/ ReleaseRouter
    \/ \E ls \in SUBSET Lanes : ForceLaneSet(ls)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : LetBackIn(b)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A b \in Bags : SF_vars(DeliverBag(b))

RouterWithinLaneCapacity == RidingCount <= CapacityOf(activeLanes)

RidingBagEventuallyLeaves ==
    \A b \in Bags : (place[b] = Riding) ~> (place[b] # Riding)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Bags = {g1, g2}
    Lanes = {l1, l2}
    PerLane = 1
    MaxEpoch = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT RouterWithinLaneCapacity
PROPERTY RidingBagEventuallyLeaves
nl:
An airport baggage router moves bags across a set of sorting lanes. The set of
lanes that are in service is decided by epoch-numbered reconfiguration: the
router holds an epoch number and the active lane set, and each lane can carry a
fixed number of bags, so the router's carrying capacity is the number of active
lanes times that per-lane figure. Every bag is in exactly one state: outside the
router, riding inside the router, held aside on the overflow spur, or delivered.

A bag that is outside can be admitted into the router as long as the bags already
riding inside, plus that one, are still within the current carrying capacity. A
bag riding inside can be delivered. A delivered bag can be recycled back to the
outside state so it can travel again.

A normal reconfiguration advances the epoch and installs a new active lane set,
but only if the bags currently riding inside would still be within the carrying
capacity that the new lane set implies; a reconfiguration that would leave the
router over capacity is simply not available. Normal reconfiguration is blocked
while the duty manager has seized the router.

The duty manager holds a privileged override. The manager can seize the router
and release it again. While the router is seized, the manager can force any lane
set into service without advancing the epoch at all; because a forced
installation ignores the capacity arithmetic, it first sweeps every bag riding
inside the router onto the overflow spur, so the router is empty at the moment
the new lane set takes effect. A bag on the overflow spur can be let back into
the router whenever the current capacity has room for it.

The complete set of actions is: admit an outside bag into the router, deliver a
bag riding inside, recycle a delivered bag back to the outside, reconfigure
normally with an epoch advance, seize the router as duty manager, release the
router, force a lane set into service by override while sweeping the router onto
the overflow spur, and let a bag back in from the overflow spur.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of bags riding inside the router never exceeds the
number of active lanes times the per-lane bag figure, through every normal
reconfiguration and every forced override installation.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: every bag that is riding inside the router eventually stops
riding inside it.

---- MODULE W4Od3m8p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Desks, Parties, MaxSeq

FreeLock == "free"
NoReservation == [party |-> "noparty", seq |-> 0]

VARIABLES batchLock, posLock, applied, cursor, reservation

vars == <<batchLock, posLock, applied, cursor, reservation>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ batchLock \in Desks \union {FreeLock}
    /\ posLock \in [Parties -> Desks \union {FreeLock}]
    /\ applied \in [Parties -> SUBSET (1..MaxSeq)]
    /\ cursor \in [Parties -> 0..MaxSeq]
    /\ reservation \in [Desks -> {NoReservation} \union
                                 [party : Parties, seq : 1..MaxSeq]]

HoldsAFineLock(d) == \E p \in Parties : posLock[p] = d

Init ==
    /\ batchLock = FreeLock
    /\ posLock = [p \in Parties |-> FreeLock]
    /\ applied = [p \in Parties |-> {}]
    /\ cursor = [p \in Parties |-> 0]
    /\ reservation = [d \in Desks |-> NoReservation]

TakeBatchLock(d) ==
    /\ batchLock = FreeLock
    /\ reservation[d] = NoReservation
    /\ batchLock' = d
    /\ UNCHANGED <<posLock, applied, cursor, reservation>>

ReserveNext(d, p) ==
    /\ batchLock = d
    /\ posLock[p] = FreeLock
    /\ reservation[d] = NoReservation
    /\ cursor[p] < MaxSeq
    /\ posLock' = [posLock EXCEPT ![p] = d]
    /\ reservation' = [reservation EXCEPT ![d] =
                        [party |-> p, seq |-> cursor[p] + 1]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchLock, applied, cursor>>

ApplyReservation(d) ==
    /\ reservation[d] # NoReservation
    /\ posLock[reservation[d].party] = d
    /\ reservation[d].seq = cursor[reservation[d].party] + 1
    /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![reservation[d].party] =
                    applied[reservation[d].party] \union {reservation[d].seq}]
    /\ cursor' = [cursor EXCEPT ![reservation[d].party] = reservation[d].seq]
    /\ posLock' = [posLock EXCEPT ![reservation[d].party] = FreeLock]
    /\ reservation' = [reservation EXCEPT ![d] = NoReservation]
    /\ UNCHANGED batchLock

AbandonReservation(d) ==
    /\ reservation[d] # NoReservation
    /\ reservation[d].seq # cursor[reservation[d].party] + 1
    /\ posLock' = [posLock EXCEPT ![reservation[d].party] = FreeLock]
    /\ reservation' = [reservation EXCEPT ![d] = NoReservation]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchLock, applied, cursor>>

DropBatchLock(d) ==
    /\ batchLock = d
    /\ reservation[d] = NoReservation
    /\ ~HoldsAFineLock(d)
    /\ batchLock' = FreeLock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<posLock, applied, cursor, reservation>>

AdminMergeNext(p) ==
    /\ cursor[p] < MaxSeq
    /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![p] = applied[p] \union {cursor[p] + 1}]
    /\ cursor' = [cursor EXCEPT ![p] = cursor[p] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchLock, posLock, reservation>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Desks : TakeBatchLock(d)
    \/ \E d \in Desks, p \in Parties : ReserveNext(d, p)
    \/ \E d \in Desks : ApplyReservation(d)
    \/ \E d \in Desks : AbandonReservation(d)
    \/ \E d \in Desks : DropBatchLock(d)
    \/ \E p \in Parties : AdminMergeNext(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AppliedSetIsExactRun == \A p \in Parties : applied[p] = 1..cursor[p]

====
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch maintains one shared record per counterparty:
the set of numbered adjustments that have been merged into that counterparty's
net position, together with a cursor giving the highest adjustment number the
position is known to have taken. Access is protected by hierarchical locks: one
coarse lock on the whole batch, and inside it a fine lock on each counterparty's
position.

A desk with no reservation outstanding takes the batch's coarse lock. Holding the
coarse lock and carrying no reservation, a desk takes the fine lock on a
counterparty whose cursor has room left and in the same step reserves that
counterparty's next adjustment number, computed as one past the cursor. The fine
lock stays held across the reservation.

Applying is the step that writes: the desk merges its reserved adjustment number
into the counterparty's applied set, moves that counterparty's cursor up to the
number just applied, and releases the fine lock. A desk may only apply while its
reserved number is still exactly one past the counterparty's cursor; if the
cursor has moved on underneath it, the reservation is stale and the desk must
abandon it instead, releasing the fine lock and writing nothing. A desk holding
the coarse lock with no reservation and no fine lock can drop the coarse lock.

The settlement administrator holds a privileged override: the administrator can
merge a counterparty's next adjustment number straight into its applied set and
move its cursor up, ignoring both the coarse lock and the fine lock entirely. This
is exactly what can leave a desk's reservation stale.

The complete set of actions is: take the batch's coarse lock, take a
counterparty's fine lock and reserve its next adjustment number, apply a
reservation that is still exactly one past the cursor, abandon a stale
reservation, drop the coarse lock, and merge a counterparty's next adjustment by
administrator override.

SAFETY PROPERTY: for every counterparty the set of adjustment numbers merged into
its position is exactly the run of numbers from one up to its cursor, so no
adjustment below the cursor has ever been lost by one writer overwriting
another's work.

---- MODULE W4Od2m0p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Bays, MaxVersion

Controllers == {"north", "south"}
NoRead == [free |-> {}, version |-> -1]

VARIABLES pool, readOf, granted, retried

vars == <<pool, readOf, granted, retried>>

Reads == {NoRead} \union [free : SUBSET Bays, version : 0..MaxVersion]

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in [free : SUBSET Bays, version : 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ readOf \in [north : Reads, south : Reads]
    /\ granted \in [north : SUBSET Bays, south : SUBSET Bays]
    /\ retried \subseteq Controllers

Init ==
    /\ pool = [free |-> Bays, version |-> 0]
    /\ readOf = [north |-> NoRead, south |-> NoRead]
    /\ granted = [north |-> {}, south |-> {}]
    /\ retried = {}

ReadPool(i) ==
    /\ readOf[i] = NoRead
    /\ readOf' = [readOf EXCEPT ![i] = pool]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, granted, retried>>

ClaimBay(i, b) ==
    /\ readOf[i] # NoRead
    /\ readOf[i].version = pool.version
    /\ pool.version < MaxVersion
    /\ b \in readOf[i].free
    /\ pool' = [free |-> pool.free \ {b}, version |-> pool.version + 1]
    /\ granted' = [granted EXCEPT ![i] = granted[i] \union {b}]
    /\ readOf' = [readOf EXCEPT ![i] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED retried

DiscardRead(i) ==
    /\ readOf[i] # NoRead
    /\ \/ readOf[i].version # pool.version
       \/ readOf[i].free = {}
       \/ pool.version = MaxVersion
    /\ readOf' = [readOf EXCEPT ![i] = NoRead]
    /\ retried' = retried \union {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, granted>>

ReleaseBay(i, b) ==
    /\ b \in granted[i]
    /\ pool.version < MaxVersion
    /\ granted' = [granted EXCEPT ![i] = granted[i] \ {b}]
    /\ pool' = [free |-> pool.free \union {b}, version |-> pool.version + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<readOf, retried>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Controllers : ReadPool(i)
    \/ \E i \in Controllers, b \in Bays : ClaimBay(i, b)
    \/ \E i \in Controllers : DiscardRead(i)
    \/ \E i \in Controllers, b \in Bays : ReleaseBay(i, b)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A i \in Controllers : SF_vars(\E b \in Bays : ClaimBay(i, b))
    /\ \A i \in Controllers : SF_vars(DiscardRead(i))

    \A i \in Controllers : (readOf[i] # NoRead) ~> (readOf[i] = NoRead)

CONSTANTS
    Bays = {b1, b2}
    MaxVersion = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoBayGrantedTwice
PROPERTY ReadEventuallyResolved
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet is run by two independent control instances, the north
aisle controller and the south aisle controller, which share one pool of charging
bays. The pool is published as a register holding the set of bays currently free
together with a version number, and every write to the register bumps the version
until the version counter is exhausted. Each controller keeps its own set of bays
it has been granted.

A controller with no read outstanding reads the pool register, keeping both the
free set and the version it saw. It then tries to claim one of the bays its read
showed as free. The claim is optimistic: it lands only if the version the
controller read is still the register's current version, which is what stops the
two independent controllers from both spending the same free bay out of the same
stale picture. A landed claim removes the bay from the register's free set, bumps
the version, and adds the bay to the claiming controller's granted set.

A controller discards its read and starts over when the version has moved on,
when its read showed no free bays at all, or when the version counter is
exhausted so no claim could be written; a controller that has had to start over
is noted as having retried. A controller can release one of its granted bays,
which takes the bay out of that controller's granted set and puts it back into
the register's free set with another versioned write.

The complete set of actions is: read the pool register, optimistically claim a
bay that the read showed free while the version still matches, discard a stale,
empty or unwritable read, and release a granted bay back into the pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the north controller's granted bays and the south controller's
granted bays never overlap, so the two independent instances are never both
allocated the same charging bay.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: a controller that has a read outstanding eventually resolves
it, either by landing a claim or by discarding the read.

CONSTANTS
    Operators = {o1, o2}
    TotalSheets = 3
    LeaseSpan = 2
    MaxCapacity = 3
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT SheetsConserved
nl:
A print shop job spooler tracks every sheet of paper the shop owns. Each sheet is
in exactly one of four places at any instant: in the paper store, in the tray of
whoever currently holds the store's lease, already printed, or spoiled.

Access to the store is by lease. A lease names an operator and carries a number
of ticks left to run; when no operator holds the lease, any operator can be
granted it with a full span of ticks. A tick of the shop clock runs one tick off
a lease that still has ticks left, and a lease that has run out of ticks can be
dropped, freeing the lease for the next operator.

While holding a lease that still has ticks left, an operator can draw a sheet out
of the store into its tray. A sheet in the tray can be printed, which moves it
into the printed total. A sheet in the tray can instead be returned to the store,
but only if the store's occupancy after the return would still be within the
store's current shelf capacity. A tray sheet that the store cannot take back
because it is at or over capacity is spoiled instead.

The shop's shelf capacity changes at runtime as racking is added or pulled out.
Capacity governs returns only: shrinking it never throws sheets out of the store,
it only blocks sheets from coming back.

The complete set of actions is: grant the store lease to an operator, tick a
running lease down, drop a lease that has run out, draw a sheet from the store
into the tray, print a tray sheet, return a tray sheet to the store when capacity
allows, spoil a tray sheet that capacity will not take back, and set the shelf
capacity to a new value.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the sheets in the store, the sheets in the tray, the sheets
already printed, and the sheets spoiled always sum to exactly the shop's total
sheet count, so no lease expiry or capacity change ever creates or destroys a
sheet.

CONSTANTS Units, Fridges, MaxSlots, MaxEpoch

Bench == "bench"
WrittenOff == "writtenoff"
Away == "away"

VARIABLES epoch, commissioned, place, slotFigure

vars == <<epoch, commissioned, place, slotFigure>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ commissioned \subseteq Fridges
    /\ place \in [Units -> Fridges \union {Bench, WrittenOff, Away}]
    /\ slotFigure \in 0..MaxSlots

Inside(f) == Cardinality({u \in Units : place[u] = f})
AllowedIn(f) == IF f \in commissioned THEN slotFigure ELSE 0

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ commissioned = Fridges
    /\ place = [u \in Units |-> Away]
    /\ slotFigure = MaxSlots

Reconfigure(cs) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ cs # commissioned
    /\ \A f \in Fridges : f \notin cs => Inside(f) = 0
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ commissioned' = cs
    /\ UNCHANGED <<place, slotFigure>>

SetSlotFigure(k) ==
    /\ k # slotFigure
    /\ \A f \in commissioned : Inside(f) <= k
    /\ slotFigure' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, commissioned, place>>

AcceptUnit(u, f) ==
    /\ place[u] = Away
    /\ f \in commissioned
    /\ Inside(f) < slotFigure
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![u] = f]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, commissioned, slotFigure>>

PullToBench(u) ==
    /\ place[u] \in Fridges
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![u] = Bench]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, commissioned, slotFigure>>

PlaceFromBench(u, f) ==
    /\ place[u] = Bench
    /\ f \in commissioned
    /\ Inside(f) < slotFigure
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![u] = f]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, commissioned, slotFigure>>

WriteOffUnit(u) ==
    /\ place[u] = Bench
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![u] = WrittenOff]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, commissioned, slotFigure>>

ClearWrittenOff(u) ==
    /\ place[u] = WrittenOff
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![u] = Away]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, commissioned, slotFigure>>

Next ==
    \/ \E cs \in SUBSET Fridges : Reconfigure(cs)
    \/ \E k \in 0..MaxSlots : SetSlotFigure(k)
    \/ \E u \in Units, f \in Fridges : AcceptUnit(u, f)
    \/ \E u \in Units : PullToBench(u)
    \/ \E u \in Units, f \in Fridges : PlaceFromBench(u, f)
    \/ \E u \in Units : WriteOffUnit(u)
    \/ \E u \in Units : ClearWrittenOff(u)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A u \in Units : SF_vars(WriteOffUnit(u))

FridgeWithinItsAllowance == \A f \in Fridges : Inside(f) <= AllowedIn(f)

BenchUnitEventuallyLeaves ==
    \A u \in Units : (place[u] = Bench) ~> (place[u] # Bench)

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Units = {u1, u2}
    Fridges = {f1, f2}
    MaxSlots = 2
    MaxEpoch = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT FridgeWithinItsAllowance
PROPERTY BenchUnitEventuallyLeaves
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker keeps its units in a set of refrigerators. Which
refrigerators are commissioned is decided by epoch-numbered reconfiguration: the
tracker holds an epoch number and the set of commissioned refrigerators, and each
commissioned refrigerator can hold up to a per-fridge slot figure. That slot
figure itself changes at runtime as shelving is swapped in and out, so capacity
moves in two independent ways. Every unit is in exactly one place: inside some
refrigerator, held on the bench, written off, or outside the bank altogether.

A reconfiguration advances the epoch and installs a new commissioned set, but it
is only available when every refrigerator being decommissioned is already empty,
so units are never stranded in a fridge that has left service. The slot figure
can be set to a new value, but only when every commissioned refrigerator's
current contents would still fit inside the new figure.

A unit from outside can be accepted into a commissioned refrigerator that has a
slot free. A unit inside a refrigerator can be pulled out onto the bench. A unit
on the bench can be placed into any commissioned refrigerator with a slot free,
or can be written off. A written-off unit can be cleared back to outside the
bank.

The complete set of actions is: reconfigure the commissioned set with an epoch
advance, set the per-fridge slot figure, accept an outside unit into a
commissioned refrigerator, pull a unit out of a refrigerator onto the bench,
place a bench unit into a commissioned refrigerator, write off a bench unit, and
clear a written-off unit back to outside.

SAFETY PROPERTY: for every refrigerator, the number of units inside it is at most
its per-fridge slot figure if it is commissioned and is zero if it is not, so
neither a reconfiguration nor a change of the slot figure ever leaves a
refrigerator holding more than it is allowed to.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: every unit sitting on the bench eventually leaves the bench.

EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Centres, Zones, MaxEpoch, MaxMovements

VARIABLES epoch, assignment, inService, authorities, movements

vars == <<epoch, assignment, inService, authorities, movements>>

Authority == [centre : Centres, zone : Zones, epoch : 0..MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ assignment \in [Centres -> SUBSET Zones]
    /\ inService \subseteq Zones
    /\ authorities \subseteq Authority
    /\ movements \in 0..MaxMovements

EntitledTo(c) == assignment[c] \cap inService

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ assignment = [c \in Centres |-> {}]
    /\ inService = Zones
    /\ authorities = {}
    /\ movements = 0

Reconfigure(asg) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ asg # assignment
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ assignment' = asg
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inService, authorities, movements>>

IssueAuthority(c, z) ==
    /\ z \in EntitledTo(c)
    /\ [centre |-> c, zone |-> z, epoch |-> epoch] \notin authorities
    /\ authorities' = authorities \union
                        {[centre |-> c, zone |-> z, epoch |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assignment, inService, movements>>

MoveTrain(a) ==
    /\ a \in authorities
    /\ a.epoch = epoch
    /\ movements < MaxMovements
    /\ movements' = movements + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assignment, inService, authorities>>

RetireAuthority(a) ==
    /\ a \in authorities
    /\ authorities' = authorities \ {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assignment, inService, movements>>

TakeOutOfService(z) ==
    /\ z \in inService
    /\ inService' = inService \ {z}
    /\ authorities' = {a \in authorities : ~(a.zone = z /\ a.epoch = epoch)}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assignment, movements>>

PutInService(z) ==
    /\ z \notin inService
    /\ inService' = inService \union {z}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assignment, authorities, movements>>

Next ==
    \/ \E asg \in [Centres -> SUBSET Zones] : Reconfigure(asg)
    \/ \E c \in Centres, z \in Zones : IssueAuthority(c, z)
    \/ \E a \in Authority : MoveTrain(a)
    \/ \E a \in Authority : RetireAuthority(a)
    \/ \E z \in Zones : TakeOutOfService(z)
    \/ \E z \in Zones : PutInService(z)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CurrentAuthoritiesStillEntitled ==
    \A a \in authorities : a.epoch = epoch => a.zone \in EntitledTo(a.centre)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Centres = {ca, cb}
    Zones = {z1, z2}
    MaxEpoch = 1
    MaxMovements = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CurrentAuthoritiesStillEntitled
nl:
A subway signalling block system divides the running lines into zones and hands
each zone to a control centre by epoch-numbered reconfiguration. The system holds
an epoch number together with the assignment, which is the set of zones given to
each control centre. Separately, the system records which zones are physically in
service; zones are taken out of service and put back at runtime as track work
comes and goes, and those changes do not touch the epoch at all.

A control centre is entitled to a zone only when that zone is both in its own
assignment and physically in service. A centre issues a movement authority naming
itself, a zone it is entitled to, and the epoch in force at that moment. An
authority whose stamped epoch is still the current epoch can be used to move a
train, which counts one movement. Any authority can be retired.

A reconfiguration advances the epoch and installs a new assignment. It leaves
authorities alone deliberately: an authority stamped with the retired epoch is
simply stale, and nothing may be done with it. Taking a zone out of service does
not advance the epoch, so it cannot rely on the epoch to invalidate anything; it
therefore revokes, in the same step, every authority for that zone that carries
the current epoch. Putting a zone back into service leaves authorities untouched.

The complete set of actions is: reconfigure the assignment with an epoch advance,
issue an authority for a zone the issuing centre is entitled to, use a
current-epoch authority to move a train, retire an authority, take a zone out of
service while revoking its current-epoch authorities, and put a zone back into
service.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every authority stamped with the current epoch names a zone that
its issuing centre is entitled to right now, meaning a zone both in that centre's
assignment and physically in service, so no centre made stale by reconfiguration
or by track work can hold an authority that still passes the check for moving a
train.

EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Installers, Doors, TotalCredits

FreeLock == "free"

VARIABLES vault, staged, issued, burned, hubLock, doorLock

vars == <<vault, staged, issued, burned, hubLock, doorLock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ vault \in 0..TotalCredits
    /\ staged \in 0..TotalCredits
    /\ issued \in 0..TotalCredits
    /\ burned \in 0..TotalCredits
    /\ hubLock \in Installers \union {FreeLock}
    /\ doorLock \in [Doors -> Installers \union {FreeLock}]

HoldsSomething(i) == hubLock = i \/ \E d \in Doors : doorLock[d] = i

Init ==
    /\ vault = TotalCredits
    /\ staged = 0
    /\ issued = 0
    /\ burned = 0
    /\ hubLock = FreeLock
    /\ doorLock = [d \in Doors |-> FreeLock]

TakeHubLock(i) ==
    /\ hubLock = FreeLock
    /\ hubLock' = i
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, staged, issued, burned, doorLock>>

TakeDoorLock(i, d) ==
    /\ hubLock = i
    /\ doorLock[d] = FreeLock
    /\ doorLock' = [doorLock EXCEPT ![d] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, staged, issued, burned, hubLock>>

DrawToHub(i) ==
    /\ hubLock = i
    /\ vault > 0
    /\ vault' = vault - 1
    /\ staged' = staged + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<issued, burned, hubLock, doorLock>>

PushToDoor(i, d) ==
    /\ doorLock[d] = i
    /\ staged > 0
    /\ staged' = staged - 1
    /\ issued' = issued + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, burned, hubLock, doorLock>>

BurnCredit ==
    /\ issued > 0
    /\ issued' = issued - 1
    /\ burned' = burned + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, staged, hubLock, doorLock>>

ReturnToVault(i) ==
    /\ hubLock = i
    /\ staged > 0
    /\ staged' = staged - 1
    /\ vault' = vault + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<issued, burned, hubLock, doorLock>>

ReleaseLocks(i) ==
    /\ HoldsSomething(i)
    /\ hubLock' = IF hubLock = i THEN FreeLock ELSE hubLock
    /\ doorLock' = [d \in Doors |->
                        IF doorLock[d] = i THEN FreeLock ELSE doorLock[d]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, staged, issued, burned>>

AdminReclaim ==
    /\ issued > 0
    /\ issued' = issued - 1
    /\ vault' = vault + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<staged, burned, hubLock, doorLock>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Installers : TakeHubLock(i)
    \/ \E i \in Installers, d \in Doors : TakeDoorLock(i, d)
    \/ \E i \in Installers : DrawToHub(i)
    \/ \E i \in Installers, d \in Doors : PushToDoor(i, d)
    \/ BurnCredit
    \/ \E i \in Installers : ReturnToVault(i)
    \/ \E i \in Installers : ReleaseLocks(i)
    \/ AdminReclaim

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A i \in Installers : SF_vars(ReleaseLocks(i))

HubLockEventuallyReleased ==
    \A i \in Installers : (hubLock = i) ~> (hubLock # i)

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Installers = {i1, i2}
    Doors = {dv1, dv2}
    TotalCredits = 3
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CreditsConserved
PROPERTY HubLockEventuallyReleased
nl:
A smart-home door lock network issues access credits to its locks. Every credit
the household owns is in exactly one of four places at any instant: sitting in
the vault, staged in the hub's buffer, issued out to the lock devices, or burned
by an unlock that has already happened.

Moving credits is protected by hierarchical locks. There is one coarse lock on
the hub, and inside it a fine lock on each individual door device. An installer
with the hub's coarse lock can draw a credit out of the vault into the hub buffer
and can put a staged credit back into the vault. To push a staged credit out to a
particular door, the installer must additionally hold that door's fine lock,
which it can only take while it holds the hub lock. An installer can release
everything it holds, dropping the hub lock and every door lock it is holding, in
one step. A credit that has been issued out to the doors is burned when someone
actually unlocks a door.

The household administrator has a privileged override: the administrator can pull
an issued credit straight back into the vault, holding neither the hub lock nor
any door lock.

The complete set of actions is: take the hub's coarse lock, take a door's fine
lock while holding the hub lock, draw a credit from the vault into the hub
buffer, push a staged credit out to a door whose fine lock is held, burn an
issued credit on an unlock, put a staged credit back into the vault, release
every lock an installer holds, and pull an issued credit back to the vault by
administrator override.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the credits in the vault, the credits staged in the hub buffer,
the credits issued out to the doors, and the credits already burned always sum to
exactly the household's total credit count, so no lock handover or administrator
override ever creates or destroys a credit.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: an installer that holds the hub's coarse lock eventually stops
holding it.

---- MODULE W4Od11m6p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Operators, SpoolSize, MaxLeaseSize, LeaseSpan, MaxCollections

Slack == SpoolSize + MaxLeaseSize

VARIABLES reserved, lease, seized, collected

vars == <<reserved, lease, seized, collected>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ reserved \in 0..Slack
    /\ lease \in [Operators -> [size : 0..MaxLeaseSize, ticks : 0..LeaseSpan]]
    /\ seized \in BOOLEAN
    /\ collected \in 0..MaxCollections

Init ==
    /\ reserved = 0
    /\ lease = [o \in Operators |-> [size |-> 0, ticks |-> 0]]
    /\ seized = FALSE
    /\ collected = 0

GrantLease(o, s) ==
    /\ ~seized
    /\ lease[o].size = 0
    /\ reserved + s <= SpoolSize
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![o] = [size |-> s, ticks |-> LeaseSpan]]
    /\ reserved' = reserved + s
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seized, collected>>

TickLease(o) ==
    /\ lease[o].ticks > 0
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![o] = [size |-> lease[o].size,
                                      ticks |-> lease[o].ticks - 1]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, seized, collected>>

HandBackLease(o) ==
    /\ lease[o].size > 0
    /\ lease[o].ticks > 0
    /\ reserved' = reserved - lease[o].size
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![o] = [size |-> 0, ticks |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seized, collected>>

ReapExpiredLease(o) ==
    /\ lease[o].size > 0
    /\ lease[o].ticks = 0
    /\ collected < MaxCollections
    /\ reserved' = reserved - lease[o].size
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![o] = [size |-> 0, ticks |-> 0]]
    /\ collected' = collected + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED seized

SeizeSpooler ==
    /\ ~seized
    /\ seized' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, lease, collected>>

ReleaseSpooler ==
    /\ seized
    /\ seized' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, lease, collected>>

AdminTopUp(o, x) ==
    /\ seized
    /\ lease[o].size > 0
    /\ lease[o].size + x <= MaxLeaseSize
    /\ reserved + x <= SpoolSize
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![o] = [size |-> lease[o].size + x,
                                      ticks |-> lease[o].ticks]]
    /\ reserved' = reserved + x
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seized, collected>>

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Operators, s \in 1..MaxLeaseSize : GrantLease(o, s)
    \/ \E o \in Operators : TickLease(o)
    \/ \E o \in Operators : HandBackLease(o)
    \/ \E o \in Operators : ReapExpiredLease(o)
    \/ SeizeSpooler
    \/ ReleaseSpooler
    \/ \E o \in Operators, x \in 1..MaxLeaseSize : AdminTopUp(o, x)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ReservedWithinSpoolSize == reserved <= SpoolSize

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Operators = {o1, o2}
    SpoolSize = 2
    MaxLeaseSize = 2
    LeaseSpan = 1
    MaxCollections = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ReservedWithinSpoolSize
nl:
A print shop job spooler hands out spool space under leases. The shop tracks one
figure, the total spool space currently reserved, and each operator holds at most
one lease, recorded as the size it reserves together with the number of ticks it
has left to run. A lease of size zero means the operator holds no lease at all.

An operator with no lease can be granted one of any size, provided the space
already reserved plus that size is still within the spool's size; the grant adds
the size to the reserved figure and starts the lease with a full span of ticks.
Granting is blocked while the shop administrator has seized the spooler. A tick
of the shop clock runs one tick off a lease that still has ticks left.

An operator can hand back a lease that is still running, which subtracts its size
from the reserved figure and clears the lease. A lease that has run out of ticks
is not cleared by itself: the reaper has to collect it, which likewise subtracts
its size from the reserved figure, clears the lease, and counts one collection.
Until the reaper gets to it, an expired lease is still holding its reservation.

The shop administrator has a privileged override. The administrator can seize the
spooler and release it again. While the spooler is seized, the administrator can
top up an operator's existing lease by an extra amount, which the ordinary grant
path cannot do because it only ever hands a lease to an operator that has none;
the top-up adds the extra to that lease's size and to the reserved figure, and it
is still only available while the reserved figure plus the extra is within the
spool's size.

The complete set of actions is: grant a lease to an operator with none, tick a
running lease down, hand back a running lease, collect an expired lease with the
reaper, seize the spooler as administrator, release the spooler, and top up an
existing lease by administrator override.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the total spool space recorded as reserved never exceeds the
spool's size, whether space is being handed out by the ordinary grant path or
topped up by the administrator, and whether or not the reaper has caught up with

    /\ proposal = NoProposal

    /\ inflight = {}

    /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ proposal' = [base |-> record, round |-> round + 1]
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, inflight>>

CastVote(b) ==

    /\ ~VoteTravelling(b)
    /\ b \notin tally
    /\ inflight' = inflight \union {[by |-> b, round |-> round]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, round, proposal, tally>>

    /\ m.round = round
    /\ proposal # NoProposal
    /\ tally' = tally \union {m.by}

    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, round, proposal>>

    /\ m \in inflight
    /\ \/ m.round # round
       \/ proposal = NoProposal
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}

    /\ Majority
    /\ record < MaxValue
    /\ record' = proposal.base + 1
    /\ proposal' = NoProposal
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, inflight>>

AbandonProposal ==
    /\ proposal # NoProposal
    /\ proposal' = NoProposal
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, round, inflight>>

    /\ record < MaxValue
    /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ record' = record + 1
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ proposal' = NoProposal
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED inflight

    /\ proposal = NoProposal
    /\ inflight = {}
    /\ round' = 0
    /\ record' = 0
    /\ tally' = {}

    \/ \E b \in Banks : CastVote(b)
    \/ \E m \in Ballots : CountVote(m)
    \/ \E m \in Ballots : DiscardVote(m)

    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A b \in Banks :

CONSTANTS
    Banks = {n1, n2, n3}
    MaxValue = 2
    MaxRound = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ProposalAtMajorityIsFresh
PROPERTY VoteEventuallyLeavesFlight
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch keeps one shared record, the batch's running
net position, and every ordinary write to it needs a quorum of the clearing banks
to vote in favour. The batch also holds a round number and, while a write is
being decided, a proposal recording the value of the record the proposer read
together with the round the proposal belongs to.

When no proposal is outstanding and rounds remain, a proposal is raised: the
round advances, the proposal records the record's present value as its base, and
the tally of votes starts empty. A bank with no vote already travelling and not
already counted can cast a vote for the outstanding proposal, stamped with the
round in force when it cast. Votes travel on a channel with no ordering
guarantee, so a cast vote sits in flight and is picked up whenever the batch gets
to it. A vote picked up while its stamped round is still the current round and a
proposal is outstanding is added to the tally; a vote whose round has moved on,
or that arrives with no proposal outstanding, is discarded.

Once the tally is a strict majority of the clearing banks, the proposal is
applied: the record takes the proposal's base plus one, and the proposal and its
tally are cleared. An outstanding proposal can also be abandoned, clearing it and
its tally without writing.

Separately, the batch runs a netting sweep that writes the record directly
without any vote at all. Because a sweep moves the record underneath anything
being decided, it advances the round and clears the outstanding proposal and its
tally in the same step. Finally, when the rounds are used up, no proposal is
outstanding and no vote is in flight, the batch closes and the next batch opens
with the round number and the record back at zero.

The complete set of actions is: raise a proposal, cast a vote for the outstanding
proposal, pick up a vote and add it to the tally, discard a vote whose round has
moved on, apply a proposal that has reached a majority, abandon an outstanding
proposal, run a netting sweep that writes the record and invalidates the
proposal, and close the batch and open the next one.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the outstanding proposal has reached a majority of
votes, the value it recorded as its base is still the record's present value, so
a proposal can never be applied on top of a write that landed after the proposal
was raised.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: a bank that has a vote in flight eventually has no vote in
flight.

    /\ assignedTo \in [Stations -> Slots \union {NoSlot}]

    /\ assignedTo' = [assignedTo EXCEPT ![token] = sl]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, inService>>

    /\ assignedTo' = [assignedTo EXCEPT ![token] = NoSlot]

    RingSize = 3
    Slots = {sl1, sl2}
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT RegistryMatchesStationRecord
nl:
A print shop job spooler allocates spool slots to its stations. The stations sit
in a fixed ring and a single token circulates; only the station currently holding
the token may change any allocation. The spooler keeps a registry saying, for
each slot, which station it is allocated to or that it is unallocated, and each
station separately records the slot it has been assigned, or that it has none.

Which slots are in service changes at runtime as spool trays are racked in and
pulled out. The token can be passed on to the next station in the ring at any
time.

The station holding the token can allocate itself an in-service slot that the
registry shows as unallocated, provided it has no slot of its own already; the
allocation writes the station into the registry for that slot and records the
slot against the station. The station holding the token can release the slot
recorded against it, which clears the registry entry and the station's own
record.

Taking a slot out of service is not gated on the token at all, because racking
work happens whether or not the ring is turning. It removes the slot from the
in-service set and revokes any allocation on it in the same step, clearing both
the registry entry for that slot and the record held by whichever station the
registry named. Putting a slot back into service leaves the registry alone.

The complete set of actions is: pass the token to the next station in the ring,
allocate an unallocated in-service slot to the token holder, release the token
holder's slot, take a slot out of service while revoking its allocation on both
sides, and put a slot back into service.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a station has a slot recorded against it, the
spooler's registry allocates that very slot to that very station, so no slot is
ever recorded against two different stations at once.

    Supervisors = {v1, v2, v3}
    Cars = {r1, r2}
    MaxMandate = 2

INVARIANT QuorumCommandIsFromEntitledInstance
PROPERTY SupersededCommandEventuallyDropped
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper is driven by two independent dispatch instances,
the tower A controller and the tower B controller, which share one pool of cars.
Only one instance is entitled to command the pool at a time, and that entitlement
carries a mandate number that advances every time the entitlement is handed over.
Handing over the mandate deliberately leaves any command already under
consideration exactly where it is, relying on the mandate number rather than on
tidying up.

Every command needs a quorum of the bank's supervisors to approve it. When no
command is under consideration, the entitled instance can propose one: it names
itself, the mandate in force, and a car the pool shows as free, and the approval
tally starts empty. Any supervisor that has not already approved the command
under consideration can approve it.

A command is executed only when its tally is a strict majority of the supervisors
and the mandate it names is still the current mandate; executing gives the named
car to the proposing instance and clears the command and its tally. A command
whose mandate has been superseded is dropped, clearing it and its tally without
doing anything to the cars. A car owned by either instance can be released back
to the free pool.

The complete set of actions is: hand the mandate over to an instance, propose a
command for a free car as the entitled instance, approve the command under
consideration as a supervisor, execute a command that has a majority and a
current mandate, drop a command whose mandate has been superseded, and release an
owned car back to the pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the command under consideration has a majority of
approvals and names the current mandate, the instance that proposed it is the
instance currently entitled to command, so a superseded instance's command can
never pass the check that lets it take a car.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: a command whose mandate has been superseded is eventually
dropped.

---- MODULE W4Od15m7p3t0 ----

CONSTANTS Firms, Slots, MaxGen

FreeSlot == "free"
NoTicket == [slot |-> "noslot", gen |-> -1]

VARIABLES slotReg, ticket, crashed, printed

vars == <<slotReg, ticket, crashed, printed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ slotReg \in [Slots -> [holder : Firms \union {FreeSlot}, gen : 0..MaxGen]]
    /\ ticket \in [Firms -> {NoTicket} \union [slot : Slots, gen : 0..MaxGen]]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Firms
    /\ printed \subseteq Slots

TicketCurrent(f) ==
    /\ ticket[f] # NoTicket
    /\ ticket[f].gen = slotReg[ticket[f].slot].gen

Init ==
    /\ slotReg = [s \in Slots |-> [holder |-> FreeSlot, gen |-> 0]]
    /\ ticket = [f \in Firms |-> NoTicket]
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ printed = {}

SwapIntoSlot(f, s) ==
    /\ f \notin crashed
    /\ ticket[f] = NoTicket
    /\ slotReg[s].holder = FreeSlot
    /\ slotReg[s].gen < MaxGen
    /\ slotReg' = [slotReg EXCEPT ![s] =
                    [holder |-> f, gen |-> slotReg[s].gen + 1]]
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![f] =
                    [slot |-> s, gen |-> slotReg[s].gen + 1]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, printed>>

CrossSlot(f) ==
    /\ f \notin crashed
    /\ TicketCurrent(f)
    /\ slotReg[ticket[f].slot].holder = f
    /\ printed' = printed \union {ticket[f].slot}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotReg, ticket, crashed>>

SwapSlotFree(f) ==
    /\ f \notin crashed
    /\ TicketCurrent(f)
    /\ slotReg[ticket[f].slot].holder = f
    /\ slotReg[ticket[f].slot].gen < MaxGen
    /\ slotReg' = [slotReg EXCEPT ![ticket[f].slot] =
                    [holder |-> FreeSlot,
                     gen |-> slotReg[ticket[f].slot].gen + 1]]
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![f] = NoTicket]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, printed>>

ThrowAwayStaleTicket(f) ==
    /\ ticket[f] # NoTicket
    /\ ~TicketCurrent(f)
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![f] = NoTicket]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotReg, crashed, printed>>

CrashSilently(f) ==
    /\ f \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \union {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotReg, ticket, printed>>

WatchdogFreeSlot(s) ==
    /\ slotReg[s].holder \in crashed
    /\ slotReg[s].gen < MaxGen
    /\ slotReg' = [slotReg EXCEPT ![s] =
                    [holder |-> FreeSlot, gen |-> slotReg[s].gen + 1]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ticket, crashed, printed>>

RestartFirm(f) ==
    /\ f \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotReg, ticket, printed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Firms, s \in Slots : SwapIntoSlot(f, s)
    \/ \E f \in Firms : CrossSlot(f)
    \/ \E f \in Firms : SwapSlotFree(f)
    \/ \E f \in Firms : ThrowAwayStaleTicket(f)
    \/ \E f \in Firms : CrashSilently(f)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : WatchdogFreeSlot(s)
    \/ \E f \in Firms : RestartFirm(f)

    \A f \in Firms : TicketCurrent(f) => slotReg[ticket[f].slot].holder = f

====
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction allocates priority slots in the opening print to
member firms. Each slot is a small compare-and-swap register holding the firm
that owns it, or a marker saying it is free, together with a generation number
that is bumped by every write to that slot. Each firm holds at most one ticket, a
note of the slot it took and the generation the slot was at when it took it. A
ticket whose generation no longer matches its slot's generation is stale and
counts for nothing.

A firm that has not crashed and holds no ticket can compare-and-swap itself into
a free slot, provided that slot still has generations left; the swap writes the
firm as owner, bumps the slot's generation, and gives the firm a ticket at the
new generation. Holding a ticket that still matches its slot's generation and
still names it as owner, a firm can cross that slot into the opening print, and
can compare-and-swap the slot back to free, which bumps the generation again and
gives up the ticket. A firm whose ticket no longer matches its slot's generation
simply throws the ticket away.

A firm can crash silently: nothing changes anywhere, so a slot it owns stays
owned and its ticket stays as it was. The exchange's watchdog can force a slot
whose owner has crashed back to free, bumping the slot's generation, and it does
not go looking for the crashed firm's ticket, which is precisely what leaves that
ticket stale. A crashed firm can be restarted.

The complete set of actions is: compare-and-swap into a free slot, cross a slot
held on a current ticket into the opening print, compare-and-swap a held slot back
to free, throw away a stale ticket, crash a firm silently, force a crashed owner's
slot back to free with the watchdog, and restart a crashed firm.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a firm's ticket still carries its slot's current
generation, that slot's register names that very firm as owner, so two firms can
never both hold current tickets for the same priority slot.

---- MODULE W4Od17m0p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Handlers, Entries, MaxVersion

NoUpdate == [base |-> {}, version |-> -1, add |-> "noentry"]

VARIABLES record, update, retried, dropped

vars == <<record, update, retried, dropped>>

Updates == [base : SUBSET Entries, version : 0..MaxVersion, add : Entries]

TypeOK ==
    /\ record \in [contents : SUBSET Entries, version : 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ update \in [Handlers -> {NoUpdate} \union Updates]
    /\ retried \subseteq Handlers
    /\ dropped \subseteq Entries

Init ==
    /\ record = [contents |-> {}, version |-> 0]
    /\ update = [h \in Handlers |-> NoUpdate]
    /\ retried = {}
    /\ dropped = {}

ComposeUpdate(h, e) ==
    /\ update[h] = NoUpdate
    /\ update' = [update EXCEPT ![h] =
                    [base |-> record.contents,
                     version |-> record.version,
                     add |-> e]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, retried, dropped>>

ApplyUpdate(h) ==
    /\ update[h] # NoUpdate
    /\ update[h].version = record.version
    /\ record.version < MaxVersion
    /\ record' = [contents |-> update[h].base \union {update[h].add},
                  version |-> record.version + 1]
    /\ update' = [update EXCEPT ![h] = NoUpdate]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<retried, dropped>>

RejectUpdate(h) ==
    /\ update[h] # NoUpdate
    /\ \/ update[h].version # record.version
       \/ record.version = MaxVersion
    /\ update' = [update EXCEPT ![h] = NoUpdate]
    /\ retried' = retried \union {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, dropped>>

DropEntry(e) ==
    /\ e \in record.contents
    /\ record.version < MaxVersion
    /\ record' = [contents |-> record.contents \ {e},
                  version |-> record.version + 1]
    /\ dropped' = dropped \union {e}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<update, retried>>

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Handlers, e \in Entries : ComposeUpdate(h, e)
    \/ \E h \in Handlers : ApplyUpdate(h)
    \/ \E h \in Handlers : RejectUpdate(h)
    \/ \E e \in Entries : DropEntry(e)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A h \in Handlers : SF_vars(ApplyUpdate(h))
    /\ \A h \in Handlers : SF_vars(RejectUpdate(h))

FreshUpdateMatchesRecord ==
    \A h \in Handlers :
        (update[h] # NoUpdate /\ update[h].version = record.version)
            => update[h].base = record.contents

UpdateEventuallyDisposed ==
    \A h \in Handlers : (update[h] # NoUpdate) ~> (update[h] = NoUpdate)

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Handlers = {h1, h2}
    Entries = {e1, e2}
    MaxVersion = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT FreshUpdateMatchesRecord
PROPERTY UpdateEventuallyDisposed
nl:
An airport baggage router keeps one shared record: the set of routing entries
currently loaded into the sorter. The record carries a version number, and every
write to it bumps the version. Baggage handlers update it optimistically. Each
handler can have at most one update composed at a time.

Composing an update takes a full copy of the record's current contents as the
update's base, stamps it with the version the handler read, and names one routing
entry to add. Composed updates sit waiting and are picked up by the router in
whatever order it likes, with no ordering guarantee at all, so an update composed
early can easily be picked up after several later ones have already landed.

Picking up an update applies it only if the version stamped on it is still the
record's version and the version counter has room left; applying replaces the
record's contents with the update's base plus the named entry and bumps the
version. An update that cannot be applied, because the version has moved on or
the version counter is exhausted, is rejected and its handler is noted as having
had to retry. Separately, the router can drop a routing entry out of the record,
which is itself a write and so bumps the version too; every entry ever dropped
this way is noted in the router's drop log.

The complete set of actions is: compose an update naming an entry to add, apply a
composed update whose version still matches, reject a composed update that cannot
be applied, and drop a routing entry out of the record while noting it in the drop log.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every composed update whose stamped version is still the
record's current version has a base equal to the record's present contents, so an
update can never be applied on top of a write that landed after that update was
composed.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: every composed update is eventually disposed of, either
applied to the record or rejected.

stations sit in a fixed ring with a single circulating token, and only the station
holding the token may draw a chute. The router keeps a draw counter, the set of
chute numbers it has handed out so far, and, for each station, the chute number it
currently holds or zero if it holds none.

The token can be passed on to the next station in the ring at any time, and it is
passed blindly, without checking whether that station is still running. The
station holding the token, provided it has not crashed and holds no chute already
and the counter has room left, draws a chute: the draw counter goes up by one, the
new counter value is added to the set of numbers handed out, and that number is
recorded against the station. The station holding the token can give up the chute
recorded against it, which clears its record; the number stays in the set of
numbers handed out, because it really was handed out.

A station can crash silently, which changes nothing at all: it keeps whatever
chute number is recorded against it and the token stays wherever it is. A crashed
station can be restarted, and on restart it comes back with no chute recorded
against it.

The complete set of actions is: pass the token to the next station in the ring,
draw the next chute number as the token holder, give up the chute recorded against
the token holder, crash a station silently, and restart a crashed station.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the set of chute numbers the router has handed out is exactly the
run of numbers from one up to the draw counter, so the counter has never moved
twice for the same number and no chute number has been handed to two stations.

---- MODULE W4Od7m2p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Participants, Jobs

Idle == "idle"
Preparing == "preparing"
Committed == "committed"
Aborted == "aborted"

VARIABLES phase, votes, discharged, crashed

vars == <<phase, votes, discharged, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in [Jobs -> {Idle, Preparing, Committed, Aborted}]
    /\ votes \in [Jobs -> SUBSET Participants]
    /\ discharged \subseteq Jobs
    /\ crashed \subseteq Participants

Init ==
    /\ phase = [j \in Jobs |-> Idle]
    /\ votes = [j \in Jobs |-> {}]
    /\ discharged = {}
    /\ crashed = {}

BeginPreparing(j) ==
    /\ phase[j] = Idle
    /\ j \notin discharged
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = Preparing]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![j] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<discharged, crashed>>

VoteYes(p, j) ==
    /\ phase[j] = Preparing
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ p \notin votes[j]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![j] = votes[j] \union {p}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, discharged, crashed>>

CommitJob(j) ==
    /\ phase[j] = Preparing
    /\ votes[j] = Participants
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = Committed]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, discharged, crashed>>

AbortJob(j) ==
    /\ phase[j] = Preparing
    /\ crashed # {}
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = Aborted]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![j] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<discharged, crashed>>

ResetJob(j) ==
    /\ phase[j] = Aborted
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, discharged, crashed>>

PerformDischarge(j) ==
    /\ phase[j] = Committed
    /\ j \notin discharged
    /\ discharged' = discharged \union {j}
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![j] = {}]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

CrashSilently(p) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \union {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, discharged>>

RestartParticipant(p) ==
    /\ p \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, discharged>>

Next ==
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : BeginPreparing(j)
    \/ \E p \in Participants, j \in Jobs : VoteYes(p, j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : CommitJob(j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : AbortJob(j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : ResetJob(j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : PerformDischarge(j)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : CrashSilently(p)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : RestartParticipant(p)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A p \in Participants, j \in Jobs : SF_vars(VoteYes(p, j))
    /\ \A j \in Jobs : SF_vars(CommitJob(j))
    /\ \A j \in Jobs : SF_vars(AbortJob(j))

DischargedJobNotLeftCommitted ==
    \A j \in discharged : phase[j] # Committed

PreparingJobEventuallyDecided ==
    \A j \in Jobs : (phase[j] = Preparing) ~> (phase[j] # Preparing)

====
nl:
A container-ship crane yard discharges containers under a two-phase commit across
its participants: the crane cab, the yard planner and the customs desk all have to
agree before a discharge happens. Discharging is the irreversible step, and each
discharge job may be discharged at most once.

Each job is in one of four phases: idle, preparing, committed or aborted, and each
job carries the set of participants that have voted yes in its current preparing
round. A job that is idle and has not already been discharged can be moved into
preparing, which starts its vote set empty. A participant that has not crashed and
has not already voted for the job in this round can vote yes.

A preparing job whose vote set covers every participant moves to committed. A
preparing job can instead be aborted whenever some participant has crashed, which
clears its votes and puts it in the aborted phase; an aborted job can be reset back
to idle so it can be tried again.

Performing the discharge is what makes the job real. It is available only for a
committed job that has not already been discharged, and it does three things at
once: it records the job as discharged, it clears the job's votes, and it retires
the commit decision by putting the job back into the idle phase, so nothing is left
standing in the committed phase behind a job that has already gone.

A participant can crash silently, changing nothing else, and a crashed participant
can be restarted.

The complete set of actions is: move an idle undischarged job into preparing, vote
yes for a preparing job, commit a preparing job whose votes cover every
participant, abort a preparing job while some participant is crashed, reset an
aborted job to idle, perform the discharge of a committed job, crash a participant
silently, and restart a crashed participant.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no job that has already been discharged is sitting in the
committed phase, so the commit decision that authorises the irreversible discharge
is never left standing where it could authorise a second one.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: every job that is in the preparing phase eventually leaves the
preparing phase.

CONSTANTS Drones, MaxDrops

VARIABLES roster, tally, proposalOpen, crashed, drops

TypeOK ==

    /\ tally \subseteq Drones
    /\ proposalOpen \in BOOLEAN
    /\ crashed \subseteq Drones
    /\ drops \in 0..MaxDrops

QuorumReached == 2 * Cardinality(tally) > Cardinality(roster)

Init ==
    /\ roster = Drones
    /\ tally = {}
    /\ proposalOpen = FALSE
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ drops = 0

OpenProposal ==
    /\ ~proposalOpen
    /\ proposalOpen' = TRUE
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, crashed, drops>>

CastVote(d) ==
    /\ proposalOpen
    /\ d \in roster
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ d \notin tally
    /\ tally' = tally \union {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, proposalOpen, crashed, drops>>

ExecuteRelease ==
    /\ proposalOpen
    /\ QuorumReached
    /\ drops < MaxDrops
    /\ drops' = drops + 1
    /\ proposalOpen' = FALSE
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, crashed>>

CrashSilently(d) ==
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \union {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, tally, proposalOpen, drops>>

StrikeOffRoster(d) ==
    /\ d \in crashed
    /\ d \in roster
    /\ roster' = roster \ {d}
    /\ tally' = tally \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposalOpen, crashed, drops>>

EnrolOnRoster(d) ==
    /\ d \notin roster
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ roster' = roster \union {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, proposalOpen, crashed, drops>>

RestartDrone(d) ==
    /\ d \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, tally, proposalOpen, drops>>

Next ==
    \/ OpenProposal
    \/ \E d \in Drones : CastVote(d)
    \/ ExecuteRelease
    \/ \E d \in Drones : CrashSilently(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : StrikeOffRoster(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : EnrolOnRoster(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : RestartDrone(d)

nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm releases retardant only after a quorum of its
roster has voted for the release. The swarm keeps a roster, which is the set of
drones currently authorised to take part, and while a release proposal is open it
keeps a tally of the drones whose votes have been counted for that proposal. The
quorum needed is a strict majority of the current roster, so the bar moves as the
roster does.

When no proposal is open, one can be opened, which starts the tally empty. A drone
that is on the roster, has not crashed, and is not already in the tally can vote,
which adds it to the tally. Once the tally is a strict majority of the roster, the
release is executed: one retardant drop is counted, the proposal is closed and the
tally is cleared.

A drone can crash silently, which changes nothing else: it stays on the roster and
any vote of its already in the tally stays counted. Ground control can strike a
crashed drone off the roster, and striking off is not just a roster edit: it
removes the drone from the roster and from the tally in the same step, so a drone
that has lost its authorisation is not left propping up an open vote. A drone that
is off the roster and not crashed can be enrolled back onto it, and a crashed drone
can be restarted.

The complete set of actions is: open a release proposal, cast a vote as a rostered
uncrashed drone, execute the release once the tally is a majority of the roster,
crash a drone silently, strike a crashed drone off the roster and out of the tally,
enrol an uncrashed drone back onto the roster, and restart a crashed drone.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every drone counted in the open proposal's tally is on the swarm's
current roster, so no drone that has been struck off can still be counted towards
authorising a retardant release.

EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Hubs, Slots, MaxTerm

Devices == {"hallway", "garage"}
NoLeader == "noleader"

VARIABLES term, leader, freeSlots, held, inService

vars == <<term, leader, freeSlots, held, inService>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ leader \in Hubs \union {NoLeader}
    /\ freeSlots \subseteq Slots
    /\ held \in [hallway : SUBSET Slots, garage : SUBSET Slots]
    /\ inService \subseteq Slots

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ freeSlots = Slots
    /\ held = [hallway |-> {}, garage |-> {}]
    /\ inService = Slots

ElectLeader(h) ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ leader' = h
    /\ term' = IF term < MaxTerm THEN term + 1 ELSE term
    /\ UNCHANGED <<freeSlots, held, inService>>

FailLeader ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ leader' = NoLeader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, freeSlots, held, inService>>

GrantSlot(dv, s) ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ s \in freeSlots
    /\ freeSlots' = freeSlots \ {s}
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![dv] = held[dv] \union {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, inService>>

ReturnSlot(dv, s) ==
    /\ s \in held[dv]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![dv] = held[dv] \ {s}]
    /\ freeSlots' = freeSlots \union {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, inService>>

TakeOutOfService(s) ==
    /\ s \in inService
    /\ inService' = inService \ {s}
    /\ freeSlots' = freeSlots \ {s}
    /\ held' = [dv \in Devices |-> held[dv] \ {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader>>

PutInService(s) ==
    /\ s \notin inService
    /\ inService' = inService \union {s}
    /\ freeSlots' = freeSlots \union {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, held>>

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Hubs : ElectLeader(h)
    \/ FailLeader
    \/ \E dv \in Devices, s \in Slots : GrantSlot(dv, s)
    \/ \E dv \in Devices, s \in Slots : ReturnSlot(dv, s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : TakeOutOfService(s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : PutInService(s)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A dv \in Devices, s \in Slots : SF_vars(ReturnSlot(dv, s))

SlotBooksBalance ==
    Cardinality(freeSlots) + Cardinality(held.hallway) + Cardinality(held.garage)
        = Cardinality(inService)

HeldSlotEventuallyReturned ==
    \A dv \in Devices, s \in Slots : (s \in held[dv]) ~> (s \notin held[dv])
